mainTopic: Wine and bedding in the support given to a wife or widow: when wine is allowed, stories of widows asking judges for support, and the mats, pillow and cushion in the משנה's list.
overview: The גמרא rules that wine is not part of the fixed support for a wife. It learns this from חנה, whom the פסוק describes as eating but not drinking. A ברייתא says a woman used to wine does get wine. The גמרא answers in two ways: אביי's reading of שמואל, where the number of cups depends on her habit and on whether her husband is present, or that the wine is meant for cooking, as in the story of נקדימון בן גוריון's daughter-in-law. A ברייתא then describes what each extra cup of wine does to a woman. רבא limits that concern to when her husband is away, and the גמרא explains that חנה was a guest, so her husband's presence did not help. Three stories follow about widows asking judges for wine and more, including the dramatic story of חומא, אביי's widow, before רבא. Finally the גמרא explains the משנה's bedding items: mats for rope beds, and a מחלוקת over a pillow and cushion. It then begins the next item, a cap, with a question from רב פפא to אביי that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Wine is not part of a wife's set support
steps.stepSummary: The basic rule: when support is set for a wife, wine is not included.
steps.simpleTranslation: We do not set aside wines for a woman.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states a rule: when a wife's food and needs are set, wine is not one of the items.
steps.deeperAnalysis: פוסקין means fixing or allotting a set amount of support. The rule says wine is left out of that list. The rest of this section will look for a source for this rule and test it.

keyTerms.meaning: We set or allot (a fixed amount of support)

phrases.english: We do not allot wines to a woman,
phrases.notes: This is about the fixed support a husband must give his wife. Wine is not on the list.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the topic of wine within a wife's support.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Wine is not included in the support set for a wife.

steps.title: The פסוק in הושע does not mean wine
steps.stepSummary: Someone might bring a proof from הושע that women receive drink. The גמרא answers that the word there means jewelry, not wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you will say: the פסוק says 'I will go after my lovers who give me my bread and my water, my wool and my flax, my oil and my drinks.' That word means things a woman longs for. And what are they? Jewelry.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא blocks a possible challenge to the rule. It explains that a word in הושע that sounds like 'drinks' really means jewelry.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word שקויי sounds like 'drinks.' That would suggest a woman normally receives wine. The גמרא reads it as related to משתוקקת, meaning 'longs for,' so it refers to the jewelry a woman wants. The proof falls away and the rule stands.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you will say (bringing up a possible objection)
My drinks (read here as things I long for)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read 'ואם תאמר' as a new opinion. The גמרא raises a possible proof against its own rule only so it can knock it down.

phrases.english: And if you will say:
"I will go after my lovers
who give me my bread and my water,
my wool and my flax, my oil and my drinks" —
that means things a woman longs for,
phrases.notes: The גמרא connects שקויי to משתוקקת, 'longs for,' because the two words sound alike.

phrases.english: and what are they? Jewelry.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends the rule in step 1 against a possible proof from a פסוק.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects using the פסוק in הושע as proof that women are given wine.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The word שקויי does not mean drinks here. It means the jewelry a woman longs for.

steps.title: רבי יהודה's source from חנה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה learns the rule from the פסוק about חנה: it says 'he drank,' not 'she drank.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה of כפר נביריא (some say of כפר נפור חיל) taught: From where do we know that wine is not set aside for a woman? The פסוק says, 'And חנה rose after she ate in שילה and after drinking.' The form used means 'he drank,' not 'she drank.'
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא brings a positive source for the rule, a teaching about חנה at שילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says חנה ate, using a feminine form. For drinking, it uses a form that reads as masculine, 'he drank.' רבי יהודה learns that she ate but did not drink wine, so wine is not part of what a woman normally receives.

phrases.aramaic: דָּרֵשׁ רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אִישׁ כְּפַר נְבִירְיָא,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda of the village of Neviraya taught,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרִי לַהּ אִישׁ כְּפַר נְפוֹר חַיִל:
phrases.english: and some say, of the village of Nefor Chayil:
From where do we know that we do not allot wines to a woman?
As it says: "And Hannah rose
after she ate in Shiloh and after drinking."
It means "he drank," not "she drank."
phrases.notes: The drinking word is read as masculine, so אלקנה drank. חנה only ate; she did not drink wine.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defending the rule, the גמרא gives a positive source for it.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that wine is not allotted to a woman.
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמואל א 1:9 uses a feminine form for eating but a masculine form for drinking.

steps.title: Then should 'she ate' mean he did not eat?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the method: by the same logic, 'she ate' would mean that he did not eat.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if so, the פסוק says 'she ate' and not 'he ate.' Should we also say that only she ate?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions רבי יהודה's way of reading the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If every masculine or feminine form excludes the other person, then 'she ate' should mean that אלקנה did not eat. That makes no sense, so the method itself seems weak.

keyTerms.meaning: But if so (pushing an idea to an odd result)

phrases.english: But if so,
"she ate" and not "he ate" — is that really so too?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reading method used in step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה's reading of שתה versus שתת.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a gender form excludes the other person, then 'she ate' would exclude her husband from eating, which is absurd.

steps.title: Only a change in wording teaches something
steps.stepSummary: The proof comes from the פסוק switching its wording, not from the gender form alone.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learn this because the פסוק changed its wording. Since it was already talking about her, why did it switch? Learn from this: 'he drank,' not 'she drank.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by explaining what the proof really depends on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'She ate' fits the flow of the פסוק, since the פסוק is talking about חנה. So it teaches nothing about her husband. For drinking, the פסוק unexpectedly stops using the feminine form. That switch is what signals that she did not drink.
steps.whatToRemember: The proof from חנה works only because the פסוק switched from 'she' to 'he' partway through. A gender form on its own proves nothing. So the rule stands: wine is not allotted to a woman.

phrases.english: We say it because the verse changed its wording.
After all, it has been dealing with her,
so what is the reason it changed?
Learn from this: "he drank," and not "she drank."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Clarifies how the proof works: from a change in wording, not from gender alone.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It seemed the proof came from the masculine form alone, which would also make 'she ate' exclude her husband.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only the unexpected switch from feminine to masculine teaches that she did not drink.

steps.title: A woman used to wine is given wine
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says a woman who is used to wine is given wine, which seems to clash with the rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: a woman who is used to wine is given wine!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source that seems to contradict the rule that wine is not allotted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If wine is never part of a wife's support, how can a ברייתא say some women are given wine? This tests whether the rule is absolute.

keyTerms.meaning: Used to it (here, used to drinking wine)

phrases.english: They challenged: one who is used to it — we give her!
phrases.notes: 'It' is wine. A woman who is used to wine gets wine.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises a new objection to the base rule of step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that wine is not allotted to a woman.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא rules that a woman used to wine does receive it, against the general rule.

steps.title: A woman used to wine is a special case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that a woman used to wine is an exception, and quotes שמואל about how many cups she and others get.
steps.simpleTranslation: A woman who is used to wine is different. As רב חיננא בר כהנא said in the name of שמואל: one who is used to it is given one cup; one who is not used to it is given two cups.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the general rule is about ordinary women, and a woman used to wine is an exception. It supports this with שמואל's statement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule 'no wine' stays as the general category. A woman used to wine is an exception where wine is given. שמואל's numbers look surprising, since the woman who is not used to wine gets more. The גמרא will clear this up in what comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: One who is not used to it

steps.confusionAlert: Do not assume you misread שמואל: as written, the woman not used to wine gets two cups and the one used to it gets one. It sounds backwards, and the גמרא itself goes on to explain it.

phrases.english: One who is used to it is different,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַב חִינָּנָא בַּר כָּהֲנָא אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: as Rav Chinnana bar Kahana said in the name of Shmuel:
One who is used to it — we give her one cup.

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאֵינָהּ רְגִילָה — נוֹתְנִין לָהּ שְׁנֵי כּוֹסוֹת.
phrases.english: One who is not used to it — we give her two cups.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the rule: a woman used to wine is an exception.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to contradict the rule that wine is never allotted to a woman.
steps.terutzMaskana: The rule covers ordinary women; a woman used to wine is a special case, as שמואל's statement shows.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the general rule has exceptions based on the woman's habits. It also sets up שמואל's puzzling numbers, which the גמרא goes on to explain.

steps.title: What is שמואל saying?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא is puzzled by שמואל's statement about the number of cups.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is he saying?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops and asks what שמואל could possibly mean, because his words seem backwards. This sets up אביי's explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 7 quoted שמואל about how many cups a woman gets. Read plainly, his numbers seem to go against common sense. The גמרא is not rejecting שמואל. It is asking for a reading that makes sense.

keyTerms.meaning: What is he saying? (said when a statement seems to make no sense)

phrases.english: What is he saying?!
phrases.notes: This is about שמואל's words just quoted in the previous step. As written, they seem backwards.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions how to understand שמואל's statement quoted in step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's statement about the number of cups
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: As worded, his statement seems to go against logic.

steps.title: אביי explains the four cases
steps.stepSummary: אביי sorts the cases by whether she is used to wine and whether her husband is present.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said, this is what he means: A woman used to wine gets two cups when her husband is there, and one cup when he is not. A woman not used to wine gets only one cup when her husband is there, and none at all when he is not.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives the correct reading of שמואל. There are two questions: is she used to wine, and is her husband present?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The husband's presence always allows more wine, and being used to wine also allows more. Each factor adds one cup. With neither factor, she gets nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman who is used to drinking wine
In front of her husband / when her husband is there

steps.whatToRemember: More wine is allowed when her husband is with her, and more is allowed if she is used to wine.

phrases.english: Abaye said: This is what he means:
If she is used to wine, in front of her husband: two cups;

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁלֹּא בִּפְנֵי בַעְלָהּ — נוֹתְנִין לָהּ כּוֹס אֶחָד.
phrases.english: not in front of her husband: we give her one cup.

phrases.aramaic: אֵינָהּ רְגִילָה, בִּפְנֵי בַעְלָהּ — אֶלָּא כּוֹס אֶחָד,
phrases.english: If she is not used to wine, in front of her husband: only one cup;

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁלֹּא בִּפְנֵי בַעְלָהּ — אֵין נוֹתְנִין לָהּ כׇּל עִיקָּר.
phrases.english: not in front of her husband: we do not give her any at all.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the puzzle of step 8 by rereading שמואל.
steps.terutzMaskana: The number of cups depends on two factors: being used to wine and the husband being present.

steps.title: Another answer: her wine is for cooking
steps.stepSummary: A second answer to the clash with the ברייתא: a woman used to wine is given wine for a cooked dish, not for drinking.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or if you want, say: a woman used to wine is given wine for a pot dish.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a different way to solve the problem from step 6. The ברייתא that gives her wine may mean wine for cooking.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 6 asked how a woman can be given wine if women should not drink it. This answer says the rule against drinking stays as it is. The wine she receives goes into her food.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you want, say (introduces another answer)
A pot dish cooked with wine

phrases.english: And if you want, say:
If she is used to wine, we give her wine for a pot dish.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different answer to the challenge of step 6, alongside the answer of steps 7 to 9.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא lets her drink wine.
steps.terutzMaskana: The wine she gets is for cooking.

steps.title: The story of נקדימון בן גוריון's daughter-in-law
steps.stepSummary: A story shows that חכמים set aside wine for a woman's pot dishes.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said in the name of רבי יוחנן: There was a story about the daughter-in-law of נקדימון בן גוריון. חכמים set aside for her two סאה of wine for pot dishes every week. She said to them: So may you set aside for your own daughters.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up the cooking answer with a real case. חכמים gave a wealthy woman wine for cooking.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story shows that 'wine for a pot dish' was a real, known allowance. It also shows how generous the amount could be for a woman from a rich home.

keyTerms.meaning: A story / an event that happened

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: As Rabbi Abbahu said that Rabbi Yochanan said:

phrases.aramaic: מַעֲשֶׂה בְּכַלָּתוֹ שֶׁל נַקְדִּימוֹן בֶּן גּוּרְיוֹן
phrases.english: There was a story with the daughter-in-law of Nakdimon ben Guryon,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁפָּסְקוּ לָהּ חֲכָמִים סָאתַיִם יַיִן לְצִיקֵי קְדֵרָה
phrases.english: for whom the Sages set two se'ah of wine for pot dishes,
from one Shabbat eve to the next.
She said to them: So may you set for your own daughters!
phrases.notes: She meant it as a blessing of thanks.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the cooking answer of step 10.
steps.raayaObject: A woman is given wine for pot dishes.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The story told by רבי אבהו in the name of רבי יוחנן.

steps.title: Why חכמים did not answer אמן
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא adds that she was a widow waiting for a יבם, so חכמים did not say אמן to her blessing.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: She was waiting for her יבם, and they did not answer אמן after her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a detail to the story. Her blessing did not get an אמן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Her blessing wished the same situation on their daughters. She was a widow stuck waiting for a יבם, so חכמים did not want to agree to that wish.

keyTerms.meaning: A widow waiting for her late husband's brother (יבום)

phrases.english: It was taught: She was a widow waiting for her yavam,
and they did not answer amen after her.
phrases.notes: They didn't want their own daughters to end up in her sad situation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds background to the story in step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Her blessing did not get an אמן because she was a שומרת יבם.

steps.title: What happens with each cup a woman drinks
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא describes how each extra cup affects a woman.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: One cup is good for a woman. Two is a disgrace. Three, she asks for relations out loud. Four, she would even ask a donkey in the market, and she does not care.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא explaining why a woman should be careful with wine. It goes cup by cup.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One cup is fine. Each extra cup leads to more loss of self-control. This explains the worry behind limiting a woman's wine.

phrases.english: It was taught: One cup is good for a woman.
Two is a disgrace.
Three: she asks for relations out loud.
Four: she even asks a donkey in the market,
and she does not care.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a new source about the effect of wine on a woman.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One cup is fine; more cups lead to loss of self-control.

steps.title: רבא: the warning only applies when her husband is away
steps.stepSummary: רבא limits the ברייתא to when her husband is not with her.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: This was only taught when her husband is not with her. But if her husband is with her, we have no problem with it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא narrows the ברייתא. The worry only exists when her husband is away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The danger in the ברייתא is that she will look for relations improperly. If her husband is with her, that danger is gone. This matches אביי's rule that more wine is allowed in front of her husband.

keyTerms.meaning: They only taught this in the case of
We have no problem with it

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רָבָא: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא שֶׁאֵין בַּעְלָהּ עִמָּהּ.
phrases.english: Rava said: They only taught this when her husband is not with her.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל בַּעְלָהּ עִמָּהּ, לֵית לַן בַּהּ.
phrases.english: But if her husband is with her, we have no problem with it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the ברייתא of step 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The concern about drinking applies only when her husband is not with her.

steps.title: But חנה's husband was with her
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבא: חנה avoided wine even though אלקנה was with her.
steps.simpleTranslation: But חנה's husband was with her!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבא's limit using the story of חנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule that women do not drink wine was learned from חנה. She did not drink in שילה even though אלקנה was there. That seems to go against רבא, who says wine is fine when the husband is present.

phrases.english: But Hannah, her husband was with her!
phrases.notes: This goes back to step 3, where the rule was learned from the fact that חנה did not drink.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's limit from step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's statement that wine is fine when the husband is with her
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: חנה's husband was with her, yet she did not drink.

steps.title: A guest is different
steps.stepSummary: Answer: חנה was a guest away from home, where relations are not allowed. So her husband's presence did not help.
steps.simpleTranslation: A guest is different. As רב הונא said: From where do we know that a guest may not have relations? As it says: 'They rose early in the morning, bowed before ה׳, returned, and came to their house in רמה; and אלקנה knew חנה his wife, and ה׳ remembered her.' Now, yes; before, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that חנה was staying away from home. It proves from a פסוק that a guest may not have relations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's reason is that her husband is available to her. A guest away from home may not have relations, so the husband was not available. The פסוק shows they were together only after coming home.

keyTerms.meaning: A guest staying away from home

steps.whatToRemember: Wine is allowed when her husband is with her, but only if they are able to be together. חנה, as a guest, was not.

phrases.english: A guest is different.
As Rav Huna said:
From where do we know that a guest is forbidden in marital relations?
As it says: "They rose early in the morning and bowed before the Lord,
and they returned and came to their house in Ramah;

phrases.aramaic: וַיֵּדַע אֶלְקָנָה אֶת חַנָּה אִשְׁתּוֹ וַיִּזְכְּרֶהָ ה׳״,
phrases.english: and Elkanah knew Hannah his wife, and the Lord remembered her."
Now, yes; before, no.
phrases.notes: Only once they were home were they together. In שילה, as guests, they were not.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 15.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Because אלקנה was with חנה, she should have been allowed wine.
steps.terutzMaskana: As guests they could not have relations, so his presence did not remove the concern.

steps.title: אביי's widow asks רבא for food and wine
steps.stepSummary: חומא, the widow of אביי, asks רבא to set her support. He grants food but refuses wine, because אביי did not drink wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: חומא, the wife of אביי, came before רבא. She said: Set food support for me. He set it for her. She said: Set wine for me. He said: I know that נחמני (אביי) did not drink wine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a story about a widow asking the judge רבא to set her support from her late husband's estate. He gives her food but not wine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's reasoning is that a widow gets what she was used to while her husband was alive. Since he knew אביי did not drink wine, he assumed she was not used to wine either.

keyTerms.meaning: Set or fix an amount (as a judge)

phrases.english: Ḥoma, the wife of Abaye,
came before Rava.
She said to him: Set food support for me!
He set it for her.
Set wine for me!
He said to her: I know about Naḥmani
phrases.notes: The text literally says 'to him,' but רבא is answering her. נחמני is אביי.

phrases.english: that he did not drink wine.

steps.triggerLanguage: חוּמָא דְּבֵיתְהוּ דְּאַבָּיֵי אֲתַאי לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the 'used to wine' (רגילה) exception from steps 7 and 9 in a real court case: a widow's right to wine from the estate depends on whether she was used to wine.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבא gives food support but refuses wine, because the husband did not drink wine.

steps.title: חומא shows the size of the cups and her arm is uncovered
steps.stepSummary: חומא insists that אביי gave her wine in large cups. While she shows their size, her arm is uncovered, and it is as if light fills the courtroom.
steps.simpleTranslation: She said to him: By the Master's life, he used to give me wine to drink in cups as big as this. While she was showing him, her arm was uncovered, and a light fell in the courtroom.
steps.whatsHappening: חומא pushes back against רבא's reason for refusing her wine. While she demonstrates, her arm becomes uncovered, and the story describes her striking beauty.
steps.deeperAnalysis: She answers רבא directly: whatever אביי drank himself, he gave her wine, so she was used to it. The line about light in the courtroom is a picture of how beautiful she was, and it sets up what happens next.

keyTerms.meaning: By the Master's life (a respectful oath)

phrases.english: She said to him: By the Master's life,

phrases.aramaic: דַּהֲוָה מַשְׁקֵי לִי בְּשׁוּפְרָזֵי כִּי הַאי.
phrases.english: he used to give me to drink in cups as big as this.
While she was showing him,
her arm was uncovered,
and a light fell in the courtroom.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַרָה לֵיהּ: חַיֵּי דְּמָר דַּהֲוָה מַשְׁקֵי לִי בְּשׁוּפְרָזֵי כִּי הַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: She answers רבא's reason for refusing her wine.

steps.title: רבא goes home and his wife asks who was in court
steps.stepSummary: רבא goes home and asks his wife, בת רב חסדא, for relations. She senses something and asks who was in court. He tells her it was חומא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא got up, went home, and asked בת רב חסדא for relations. בת רב חסדא said to him: Who was in the courtroom just now? He said to her: חומא, the wife of אביי.
steps.whatsHappening: The story moves to רבא's home. His wife picks up from his behavior that something happened in court, and she asks about it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His unusual request makes his wife suspect that some woman was in court. When he names חומא, the story is set up for her reaction in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked her for marital relations
The daughter of רב חסדא, רבא's wife

phrases.english: Rava got up and went into his house,
and asked the daughter of Rav Ḥisda for relations.
The daughter of Rav Ḥisda said to him:
Who was in the courtroom just now?
He said to her: Ḥoma, the wife of Abaye.

steps.triggerLanguage: קָם רָבָא, עָל לְבֵיתֵיהּ תַּבְעַהּ לְבַת רַב חִסְדָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows what happened to רבא after seeing חומא in court.

steps.title: בת רב חסדא drives חומא out of מחוזא
steps.stepSummary: בת רב חסדא chases חומא, hits her with the lock of a chest, and drives her out of מחוזא, accusing her of having killed three husbands.
steps.simpleTranslation: She went out after her and hit her with the locks of a chest until she drove her out of all of מחוזא. She said to her: You already killed three, and now you come to kill another?!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא's wife chases חומא out of the city to protect her husband. This ends the story of חומא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Her words mean that three of חומא's husbands had already died, and now she might draw רבא to her as well. She sees חומא's beauty as a danger to her own husband.

keyTerms.meaning: מחוזא, the city where רבא lived

steps.confusionAlert: 'You killed three' does not mean חומא murdered anyone. It means three of her husbands had died, and אביי was the third.

phrases.english: She went out after her,
and hit her with the locks of a chest
until she drove her out of all of Meḥoza.
She said to her: You have killed three,
and now you come to kill another?!
phrases.notes: She means her own husband, רבא.

steps.triggerLanguage: נָפְקָא אַבָּתְרַהּ, מָחֲתָא לָהּ בְּקוּלְפֵי דְשִׁידָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After hearing it was חומא, רבא's wife acts against her.

steps.title: רב נחמיה gives a widow wine because the people of מחוזא drink wine
steps.stepSummary: A widow asks רב נחמיה בריה דרב יוסף for food and wine. He grants both, because the people of מחוזא drink wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: The wife of רב יוסף son of רבא came before רב נחמיה son of רב יוסף. She said: Set food support for me. He set it. She said: Set wine for me. He set it. He said to her: I know that the people of מחוזא drink wine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a second story about a widow asking for wine. This time the judge gives her wine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the reason is different from the חומא story. רב נחמיה does not ask about this husband's habits. He goes by local custom: in מחוזא, people drink wine, so she gets wine.

phrases.english: The wife of Rav Yosef, son of Rava,

phrases.aramaic: אֲתַאי לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב נְחֶמְיָה בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יוֹסֵף.
phrases.english: came before Rav Neḥemya, son of Rav Yosef.
She said to him: Set food support for me!
He set it for her.
Set wine for me! He set it for her.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לַהּ: יָדַעְנָא בְּהוּ בִּבְנֵי מָחוֹזָא
phrases.english: He said to her: I know about the people of Meḥoza
that they drink wine.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּבֵיתְהוּ דְּרַב יוֹסֵף בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבָא אֲתַאי לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב נְחֶמְיָה בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יוֹסֵף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel story where the widow is given wine, based on local custom.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A widow in מחוזא is given wine because the local people drink wine.

steps.title: A widow asks רב יוסף for wine and silk
steps.stepSummary: A widow asks רב יוסף for food, wine, and silk clothing. When he asks why she needs silk, she says it is for appearing before him and the other חכמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: The wife of רב יוסף son of רב מנשיא of דויל came before רב יוסף. She said: Set food support for me. He set it. Set wine for me. He set it. Set silk for me. He said to her: Why silk? She said to him: For you, for your friends, and for your friends' friends.
steps.whatsHappening: A third story: this widow is given food and wine, and then asks for silk clothing. רב יוסף asks why, and she explains.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Silk goes beyond basic needs, so רב יוסף asks why she needs it. Her answer is that she is the widow of a תלמיד חכם and appears among חכמים, so she should be able to dress with dignity in front of them.
steps.whatToRemember: These stories show judges deciding what a widow gets from her husband's estate. רבא looked at what the husband did, and רב נחמיה looked at local custom. The silk story shows that a respectable widow can ask for more than bare basics.

phrases.aramaic: דְּבֵיתְהוּ דְּרַב יוֹסֵף בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב מְנַשְּׁיָא מִדְּוִיל
phrases.english: The wife of Rav Yosef, son of Rav Menashya of D'vil,
came before Rav Yosef.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַרָה לֵיהּ: פְּסוֹק לִי מְזוֹנֵי! פְּסַק לַהּ.
phrases.english: She said to him: Set food support for me! He set it for her.
Set wine for me! He set it for her.
Set silk garments for me!
He said to her: Why do you need silk?
She said to him: For you, for your friends, and for your friends' friends.
phrases.notes: She means she wants to be dressed respectably when she comes before him and the other חכמים.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּבֵיתְהוּ דְּרַב יוֹסֵף בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב מְנַשְּׁיָא מִדְּוִיל אֲתַאי לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב יוֹסֵף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another parallel story that adds a request for silk on top of food and wine.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The widow receives food and wine, and she explains that she needs silk for dignity before the חכמים.

steps.title: Why does she need mats if she has a bed?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's list of bedding and asks why she needs mats on top of a bed.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said he gives her a bed and a soft mat, etc. Why does he need to give her a soft mat and a hard mat?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה about bedding and asks why mats are on the list if she is already getting a bed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A bed seems like enough to sleep on, so the mats look extra. The גמרא wants to know what job the mats do that the bed does not.

keyTerms.meaning: A mat, here the harder one

phrases.english: "And he gives her a bed and a soft mat, etc."
A soft mat and a hard mat:
Why does she need him to give them to her?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַפָּץ וּמַחְצֶלֶת לְמָה לַהּ דְּיָהֵב לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the widow stories and returns to explaining the משנה's list of support items.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the mats are for, since she already receives a bed.

steps.title: Rope beds wear her down, so she needs a mat
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא explains that the משנה is talking about places where beds are strung with ropes, which are uncomfortable.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: The משנה is speaking of a place where people fill a bed with ropes, which wears her down.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers that in some places a bed is just a frame strung with ropes, and lying on bare ropes is hard on her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So the mat is not a luxury. It works like a mattress on top of the ropes. This makes the bed actually usable.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
In a place where they are accustomed
to fill a bed with ropes,
since it wears her down.
phrases.notes: He means sleeping on bare ropes makes her suffer, so she needs a mat on top.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 23.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: In places with rope beds, the mat is needed as a mattress so the ropes do not hurt her.

steps.title: Argument over giving her a pillow and cushion
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא records a מחלוקת: the תנא קמא says she does not get a pillow and cushion, and רבי נתן says she does.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים taught: One does not give her a pillow and a cushion. In the name of רבי נתן they said: One does give her a pillow and a cushion.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that adds to the bedding list. Two opinions argue over whether a pillow and cushion are included.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a new source beyond the משנה. The argument is simple on the surface, yes or no, but the reason behind it is not given. That gap leads to the next step.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
One does not give her a pillow and a cushion.
In the name of Rabbi Natan they said:
One does give her a pillow and a cushion.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אֵין נוֹתְנִין לָהּ כַּר וָכֶסֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the mats to a related bedding question from a ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The תנא קמא says no pillow and cushion. רבי נתן says she gets them.

steps.title: Neither side makes sense in a simple case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what case they argue about. If she normally uses them, why does the תנא קמא refuse? If she does not, why does רבי נתן give them?
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case? If she is used to them, what is the reason of the תנא קמא? And if she is not used to them, what is the reason of רבי נתן?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא by showing that in both obvious cases, one of the two opinions seems to have no reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Support is normally based on what the woman is used to. If she uses pillows, she should get them. If she does not, she should not. So the גמרא needs a third case where both views make sense.

phrases.english: What are the circumstances?
If it is her usual manner,
what is the reason of the first tanna?
And if it is not her usual manner,
what is the reason of Rabbi Natan?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ברייתא quoted in step 25.
steps.kashyaTarget: The case behind the מחלוקת in the ברייתא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Whichever simple case you choose, one opinion seems to have no reason.

steps.title: He uses them, she doesn't: the תנא קמא's view
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the case is where he uses a pillow and cushion but she does not. The תנא קמא says he can just take his own bedding with him.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, the case is where he is used to them but she is not. The תנא קמא holds that he can tell her: When I leave I take them, and when I come back I bring them with me.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finds a middle case: the husband uses a pillow and cushion, but the wife does not. It then explains the תנא קמא's reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: She herself does not need them, so the only question is whether he must leave a set with her for when he visits. The תנא קמא says no, because he can carry his own bedding back and forth.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed only for this case

phrases.english: No, it is needed
for a case where it is his usual manner
but not her usual manner.
The first tanna holds that he says to her:
"When I go away, I take them,
and when I come, I bring them with me."

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא צְרִיכָא, כְּגוֹן דְּאוֹרְחֵיהּ דִּידֵיהּ וְלָאו אוֹרְחַהּ דִּידַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 26 by defining a new case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defines a new case (he uses them, she does not)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The argument must be about what she herself is used to, which leaves one side without a reason.
steps.terutzMaskana: The argument is about his needs when he visits. The תנא קמא says he brings his own bedding.

steps.title: רבי נתן: she fears he will take her bedding
steps.stepSummary: רבי נתן's reason: sometimes he arrives at dusk without his bedding, takes hers, and leaves her on the ground. So she needs an extra set.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי נתן holds she can say to him: Sometimes you happen to arrive at twilight and cannot bring them, and you will take mine and make me lie on the ground.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the answer by giving רבי נתן's reason for why she does get a pillow and cushion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי נתן agrees she does not use them herself. He worries that on some visits the husband will show up without his bedding and use hers. So an extra set protects her from sleeping on the floor.
steps.whatToRemember: Both sides agree she does not use a pillow and cushion. They argue only about whether an extra set must be left for the husband's visits. The תנא קמא says he brings his own, and רבי נתן says she needs a backup.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Natan holds that she says to him:
"Sometimes it happens that you arrive at twilight
and you are unable to bring them,
and you will take mine
and make me lie on the ground."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer begun in step 27 with רבי נתן's side.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives the reasoning for the second opinion within the same new case
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי נתן gives her a pillow and cushion so his visits will never leave her without bedding.

steps.title: Next item in the משנה: a cap
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next item in the משנה, a cap, and opens a question from רב פפא to אביי.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: And he gives her a cap. רב פפא said to אביי:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next item on the משנה's list, a cap. It is setting up a question that רב פפא is about to ask אביי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This line only opens a new topic. רב פפא's actual question comes on the next amud.

phrases.english: "And he gives her a cap."
Rav Pappa said to Abaye:

steps.triggerLanguage: וְנוֹתֵן לָהּ כִּפָּה. אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב פָּפָּא לְאַבָּיֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the bedding discussion and opens the next item in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Quotes the משנה's rule that he gives her a cap, as a setup for רב פפא's question.
